en.headline: Civil service chief will not rule out discipline if Tai Po fire report names officials
en.dek: Secretary Ingrid Yeung said a support unit is being prepared for the Public Service Commission, and direct disciplinary action remains possible if the independent panel identifies individual failings.
body: Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung Ho Poi-yan said on Saturday that senior public servants could face disciplinary action if an independent committee investigating last year’s deadly Tai Po fire names them in its forthcoming report.

The Wang Fuk Court blaze in November 2025 killed 168 people. The committee, chaired by Justice David Lok Kai-hong, is expected to submit its findings to the Chief Executive this month. Yeung told a radio programme that if the report clearly identifies an individual official and points out inadequate performance or prima facie evidence, she would not rule out launching disciplinary proceedings directly.

She added that a support unit was being established to assist the Public Service Commission should a second-tier investigation into administrative responsibilities be required. Yeung emphasised that any follow-up would depend on the content of the report.

zh.headline: 公務員事務局長：宏福苑報告若點名不排除直接紀律處分
zh.dek: 楊何蓓茵表示已準備支援小組協助公務員敍用委員會，若獨立委員會報告清晰指出個別公務員失職，不排除直接啟動紀律程序。
body: 公務員事務局局長楊何蓓茵周六表示，若調查去年宏福苑大火的獨立委員會報告點名個別公務員，當局不排除對有關官員啟動紀律處分。
2025年11月宏福苑火災造成168人死亡。由樂啟康法官擔任主席的獨立委員會預計本月向行政長官提交報告。楊何蓓茵在電台節目中指出，若報告清晰點出個別官員的不足之處或有表面證據，她不排除直接展開紀律程序。
她補充，當局正設立支援小組，以便在需要時協助公務員敍用委員會進行第二級調查，釐清行政責任。楊何蓓茵強調，具體跟進將視乎報告內容而定。
